label: The exhibition
heading: Six panels
intro: Each panel holds artworks and the science side by side — never separated. The colour tells you which register you are in: magenta is the science layer, drawn from the fluorescent tag in the Barik Lab micrographs.

panels.title: Somatosensory system
panels.text: The body’s largest sensory apparatus — the whole skin and musculature — reading mechanical, thermal and chemical signals, and holding proprioception, the sense of where the body is in space.

panels.title: Pain in the brain
panels.text: Pain is processed and ultimately felt in the brain — and it can be modulated. A person in a coma senses no pain; a soldier fights on injured; hunger can eclipse a wound. In the Barik Lab, the lateral hypothalamus emerges as a hub where emotional states — stress, anxiety — are translated, through the brainstem and spinal cord, into the modulation of pain and itch. A few hundred neurons out of billions, lit up by mouse genetics, are enough.

links.label: When pain becomes invisible — chronic pain, explained

panels.title: Opioids / poppy
panels.text: Papaver somniferum runs through Assyrian, Sumerian, Egyptian and Chinese medicine. The body also makes its own opioids, released by hard exertion.

panels.title: Overcoming
panels.text: In the trenches, in devotion and ritual, brain mechanisms defer pain in favour of something judged more urgent.

panels.title: Anxiety and depression
panels.text: Chronic pain patients often develop both. Relieving the pain often doesn’t relieve the anxiety — the pain- and anxiety-encoding regions interact, and those connections are impaired in chronic pain.

panels.title: Tactile sensation
panels.text: Touch as a social bond — a caress, petting a dog — carried by specialised cutaneous receptors connected to nerves.

inroom.label: In the room
inroom.text: The panels were first shown as physical boards, with a note at the entrance and a guest book at the end — visitors were asked to leave a mark of their own.
